earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct; attested only in 3 transcribed songs (Coblin 1979, Beckwith 2008, Hill 2017 all listed by Glottolog as a minimal description) - no phonology/stress description exists

new_statements.citation: one of the works listed for this language (see the verification note)
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: The target lists only one work, so there were no silent or not-opened works to spot-check within the list. As a supplementary check I searched the previously filed Coblin 1979 scanned in the same directory (not in the works list) for the same stress terms: 'prosodically' and 'the four-syllable prosody of the lines' (pp. 196-197) refer to line metre of the songs, 'tone' occurs only for Chinese tonal categories (ping/shang/qu) and for Kachin comparanda ('high tone', 'mid tone' in the notes); no statement about Pai-lang word stress or accent. Nothing missed.

sources.citation: Fu Maoji 傅懋勣. 1997 [written 1950]. A descriptive grammar of Lolo. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 20(1): 1-242. [Pai-lang songs: Introduction sec. 8 (p.9) and secs. 37-39 (pp.37-38).]
sources.note: Silent on Bailang prosody; notes only that character transcription is inaccurate and that ~20 lexical matches do not prove ancestry.
Nothing; summarises attestation (3 songs, 44 lines, ~134 words, 21 Chinese loans) and cites Coblin 1979, Beckwith 2008, Hill 2017 only.

sources.citation: Li Bin 李彬 & Xu Qiaoyun 许巧云. 2019. 20世纪80年代以来藏缅语《白狼歌》研究述评 [A review of research on the Tibeto-Burman 'Bailang songs' since the 1980s]. 民族学刊 Journal of Ethnology 2019(2) (serial no. 52). DOI 10.3969/j.issn.1674-9391.2019.02.009.
sources.note: No phonology of its own; summarises Ma & Dai 1982, Zhengzhang 1993, Wu Anqi 2007, Huang Zhenhua 1998, Chen & Deng 1991 etc; only '音高' hit concerns Yi lu 'dragon/tiger', not Bailang. Reference list adds Wang Jingru 1932, Chen & Deng 1979/1981/1983/1991 (book), Liu & Chen 1985, Ma Xueliang 1986, Yang Fengjiang 1987, Yang Zhaohui 1987, Huang Xilu 2001, Luo Qijun 2005 — none phonological beyond the three analyses above.
sources.venue: 民族学刊 Journal of Ethnology

sources.citation: Hill, Nathan W. 2017. Songs of the Bailang: A New Transcription with Etymological Commentary. BEFEO 103: 386-429.
sources.note: Most recent and fullest treatment of Bailang phonology (new transcription in Baxter-Sagart-style Han Chinese); would confirm definitively that nothing is said about accent. PDF is free on Persee but gated by an altcha captcha that automated download cannot pass; a browser download would take seconds.

sources.citation: Wu Anqi 吴安其. 2007. 《白狼歌》解读 [An interpretation of the Song of Bailang]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2007(6): 12-22.
sources.note: Tones only for Eastern Han Chinese and Old Burmese as coda-derived; nothing on Bailang tone count or stress; segmental notes on Bailang initials and a hypothesised *-s suffix.

sources.citation: Huang Yilu 黄懿陆. 2001. 东汉《白狼歌》是越人歌谣 [The Eastern-Han 'Bailang songs' are Yue folk songs]. 广西民族研究 Guangxi Minzu Yanjiu 2001(3) (serial no. 65), 17 pp.
sources.note: Silent; tone numbers appear only on the modern Zhuang forms.
sources.venue: 广西民族研究 Guangxi Minzu Yanjiu

sources.citation: Huang Zhenhua 黄振华. 1998. 白狼王远夷乐德歌新解 [A new interpretation of the Bailang king's songs]. 宁夏大学学报 (哲学社会科学版) 1998(3).
sources.note: Lexical Tangut-Bailang matching; no hit for any tone/stress term; no phonology section.
sources.venue: 宁夏大学学报 (哲学社会科学版)

sources.citation: Zhengzhang Shangfang 郑张尚芳. 1993. 上古缅歌──《白狼歌》的全文解读 [An archaic Burmese song: a complete decipherment of the Bailang Songs]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 1993(1): 10-21; (续) [part 2] 1993(2): 64-70, 47.
sources.note: Tone discussed only as (a) Written Burmese tone marks reinterpreted as Old Burmese laryngeal codas and (b) Chinese tonogenesis dated after Han-Wei; Bailang forms are given with -ʔ/-h/-s/-g codas matching later tone categories (e.g. p.69 '*-ih < -s [祭部(月部去声)]'). Stress/accent never mentioned. Fullest phonological treatment of Bailang anywhere, but no sentence asserting or denying tones or stress for Bailang itself.

sources.citation: Yang Zhaohui 杨照辉. 1987. “白狼歌”辨析 [An analysis of the 'Bailang songs']. 民族文学研究 Minzu Wenxue Yanjiu 1987(1), 4 pp.
sources.venue: 民族文学研究 Minzu Wenxue Yanjiu

sources.citation: Ma Xueliang 马学良 & Dai Qingxia 戴庆厦. 1982. 《白狼歌》研究 [A study of the 'Song of Bailang']. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 1982(5): 16-26.
sources.note: Silent on tone and stress for Bailang; '声调' does not occur; Chinese tone-category labels attached to character readings only.

sources.citation: Chen Zongxiang 陈宗祥 & Deng Wenfeng 邓文峰. 1979. 《白狼歌》研究述评 [Review of studies of the Bailang songs]. 西南师范学院学报 1979(4). DOI 10.13718/j.cnki.xdsk.1979.04.009.
sources.note: No phonology content on tone or stress; historical/ethnic-affiliation review.

sources.citation: Coblin, W. South. 1979. A New Study of the Pai-lang Songs. Tsing Hua Journal of Chinese Studies n.s. 12: 179-216.
sources.note: Nothing. Sections 1.2 and 2.5 treat only segmental values (initials/finals) of the Pai-lang syllables as recoverable from Eastern Han readings of the transcribing characters; 'tone' appears only for the Chinese tonal categories of those characters; 'prosody' only for the four-syllable line metre of the songs (pp.196-197). No word 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the 38 pages.
sources.venue: Tsing Hua Journal of Chinese Studies n.s

sources.citation: Thomas, F. W. 1948. Nam, an ancient language of the Sino-Tibetan borderland. (Publications of the Philological Society XIV.) London: Oxford University Press. [Pai-lang songs discussed pp.34-35, 51, 61-62.]
sources.note: Nothing on Bailang tone or stress; 'tone' does not occur in the Pai-lang passages.
